```{r ALL THE MOST UP TO DATE OUTLIER HANDLING FUNCTIONS}
# Provided a dataset, this function can identify which values are outliers based
# on the distributions of values with the same concentration and variant. I then
# provides a data frame that contains relevant information about identified
# outliers that can be used to find and replace that outlier later on

# REMEMBER: outlier imputation should be done FOLLOWING data splitting (i.e. via
# )

#' check_outliers
#'
#' @param dataset a data frame all relevant cab columns, as well as target vector and  concentration 
#' @param alpha p-value (derived from a grubb's test) below which outleirs should be removed 
#'
#' @return flag_df, a data frame containing 
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
check_outliers = function(dataset, alpha = 0.05) {
  flag_df = NULL
  current_variant = unique(dataset$target_vector)
  current_conc = unique(dataset$Conc.)
  
  cols_to_check = dataset %>% select(starts_with("cAb"))
  cab_names = colnames(cols_to_check)
  col_num = 1
  
  
  # Outlier detection with 3*sd (tukey fence) instead of grubbs test. A manual set a p-value
  # to 0.01 if a value within the array is higher or lower than 3D*mean, then
  # return 'higher' or 'lower' depending on what value is returned
  # TO DO: This should probably be a separate function that's called elsewhere
  # for (array in cols_to_check){
  #   arr_mean = mean(array, na.rm=T)
  #   arr_sd = sd(array, na.rm = T)
  #   upper_bound = arr_mean + 2*arr_sd
  #   lower_bound = arr_mean - 2*arr_sd
  #   
  #   if (lower_bound < 0){
  #     lower_bound = 0
  #   }
  #   max_val = max(array)
  #   min_val = min(array)
  #   
  #   max_test = ifelse(max_val > upper_bound, 1, 0)
  #   min_test = ifelse(min_val < lower_bound, 1, 0)
  #   
  #   if(max_val < 0){
  #     max_test = 0
  #     min_test = 0
  #   }
  #   # print(paste('max_test: ',max_test, "\n", "min_test: ", min_test))
  #   # The original function requires a p_value as a check for whether to add to 
  #   # the flag df but we can check if either of the values are true
  #   if(max_test == 1 | min_test == 1){
  #     max_dist = max_val - arr_mean
  #     min_dist = arr_mean - min_val
  #     higher_lower = ifelse(abs(max_dist) > abs(min_dist), 'higher', 'lower')
  #     
  #     flagged_cAb = cab_names[[col_num]]
  #     flag_report = data.frame(
  #       variant = current_variant,
  #       concentration = current_conc,
  #       cAb = flagged_cAb,
  #       higher_lower = higher_lower)
  #       
  #     if (is.null(flag_df)) {
  #       flag_df = flag_report
  #     }
  #     else{
  #       flag_df = bind_rows(flag_df, flag_report)
  #     }
  #   }
  #   col_num = col_num + 1
  # }
  
  for (array in cols_to_check) {
    test = grubbs.test(array, type = 10)
    test_stat = test$statistic
    test_alpha = test$p.value

    if (test_alpha <= alpha & sum(array) != 0) {
      alternative_hypo = test$alternative
      higher_or_lower = ifelse(grepl('highest', alternative_hypo), 'higher', 'lower')

      flagged_cAb = cab_names[[col_num]]
      flag_report = data.frame(
        variant = current_variant,
        concentration = current_conc,
        cAb = flagged_cAb,
        higher_lower = higher_or_lower
      )

      if (is.null(flag_df)) {
        flag_df = flag_report
      }
      else{
        flag_df = bind_rows(flag_df, flag_report)
      }
    }
    col_num = col_num + 1
  }
  return(flag_df)
}

# Provided with a data frame containing information about individual outliers (called flag_df here), it will find those outlier values and add additional information to the original flag_df, mainly the specific outlier value and the mean of the group without the outlier included
#' Title
#'
#' @param flag_df 
#' @param dataset a data frame all relevant cab columns, as well as target vector and  concentration
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
enhance_flag_df = function(flag_df, dataset){
  # Loop over all rows of flag df, then build an array row by row that contains
  # the max and mean (na.rm = T), then add that to the original data frame and 
  # return it
  num_rows = nrow(flag_df)
  enhanced_df = NULL
  for (iter in 1:num_rows){
    current_outlier_row = flag_df[iter,]
    
    current_outlier_array = dataset %>% filter(target_vector == current_outlier_row$variant,
                                               Conc. == current_outlier_row$concentration) %>% 
      select(current_outlier_row$cAb)
    
    outlier_cab = current_outlier_row$cAb
    
    outlier_col = current_outlier_array[current_outlier_row$cAb]

    if (current_outlier_row$higher_lower == 'higher'){
      # Excluding the maximum value, obtain the mean of the column
      outlier_value = max(outlier_col)
      temp_col = outlier_col[[outlier_cab]]
      arr_without_max = temp_col[temp_col <  outlier_value]
      mean_val = mean(arr_without_max, na.rm = T)
    }

    else{
      # Excluding the minimum value, obtain the mean of the column
      outlier_value = min(outlier_col)
      temp_col = outlier_col[[outlier_cab]]
      arr_without_min = temp_col[temp_col > outlier_value]
      mean_val = mean(arr_without_min, na.rm = T)
    }
    
    extra_info=data.frame(outlier_value = outlier_value,
                          mean_value = mean_val)
    extra_info$mean_value = ifelse(is.nan(extra_info$mean_value), 0, extra_info$mean_value)

    extra_info_df = bind_cols(current_outlier_row, extra_info)
    
    if (is.null(enhanced_df)){
      enhanced_df = extra_info_df
    }
    else{
      enhanced_df = bind_rows(enhanced_df, extra_info_df)
    }
  }
  return(enhanced_df)
}

# Given an enhanced flag_df and the original dataset, this function will find
# all outlier values and replace them with the mean value or NA if you'd like to
# use an alternative imputation method. It returns a dataset of the same
# dimensions as the original, with the outlier values changed.
#' Title
#'
#' @param dataset a data frame all relevant cab columns, as well as target vector and  concentration
#' @param enhanced_flag_df 
#' @param impute_method 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
replace_outliers = function(dataset, enhanced_flag_df, impute_method='mean'){
  row_numbers = 1:nrow(dataset)
  dataset = bind_cols("row_number" = row_numbers, dataset)
  matching_row_arr = list()
  
  for(i in 1:nrow(enhanced_flag_df)) {
    current_conc = enhanced_flag_df$concentration[i]
    current_variant = enhanced_flag_df$variant[i]
    outlier_col = enhanced_flag_df$cAb[i]
    outlier_val = enhanced_flag_df$outlier_value[i]
    # Replacement value can either be the mean value contained in enhanced_flag_df
    # or it can just replace with NA
    replacement_value = ifelse(impute_method=='mean', enhanced_flag_df$mean_value[i], NA)

    # Locate the subset of rows that contain the outlier value
    matching_subset = dataset %>% 
      filter(Conc. == current_conc, target_vector == current_variant)

    # Find the single row within the matching subset where the outlier col has
    # the outlier val, then take the first column (the row number) and use that
    # to set the value to the mean in the original dataset
    matching_row = as.tibble(matching_subset[matching_subset[outlier_col]==outlier_val])
    matching_row_num = as.integer(matching_subset[matching_subset[outlier_col]==outlier_val][1])
    # print(matching_row_num)
    matching_row_arr = c(matching_row_arr, matching_row_num)
    
    # cat("i:", i, ", current_conc:", current_conc, ", current_variant:",
    #     current_variant, ", current_cab:", outlier_col, ", outlier_val:", outlier_val,
    #     ", replacement_value:", replacement_value,
    #     ", matching_row_num:", matching_row_num, "\n")

    # Print the replaced row
    # print(dataset[matching_row_num, outlier_col])
    # Replace outlier value with replacement value using the row number found above
    dataset[matching_row_num, outlier_col] = replacement_value
  }
  return(list('dataset' = dataset,
              'row_nums_arr' = matching_row_arr))
}


#------------------------------------------------------------------------------#
# Outlier control function
#' main_outliers_detection_function: main wrapper function for all outlier detection
#' functions. Calls check_outliers, enhance_flag_df, and replace_outliers
#' @param dataset a data frame all relevant cab columns, as well as target vector and  concentration
#' @param threshold p-value (from a grubb's test) below which outliers should be considered a statistical outlier 
#' @param impute imputations method to use, currently supports mean imputation 
#'
#' @return
#' @export
#'
#' @examples
main_outliers_detection_function = function(dataset, threshold, impute = 'mean') {
  
  outlier_test_df_list = dataset %>% filter(Conc. > threshold) %>% group_by(Conc., target_vector) %>% group_split()
  flag_df = NULL
  
  for (df in outlier_test_df_list) {
    outlier_check = check_outliers(df)
    
    if (is.null(flag_df)) {
      flag_df = outlier_check
    }
    
    else{
      flag_df = bind_rows(flag_df, outlier_check)
    }
  }
  # Add specific outlier value and mean value of outlier group without the outlier
  # value to the flag_df
  print(flag_df)
  enhanced_flag_df = enhance_flag_df(flag_df, dataset)
  
  # Now that we've returned a more robust version of the flag_df, we can use that
  # information to iterate over the entire data set and replace outlier values 
  # with either the mean value of their group or with NA (for MICE)
  
  outlier_removed_df = replace_outliers(dataset, enhanced_flag_df, impute_method=impute)
  outlier_removed_df = outlier_removed_df$dataset %>% select(-row_number)
  return(outlier_removed_df)
}
```

```{r Dose respons visualization}
DR_Viz = function(dataset){
  std.err = function(x, na.rm = T) sd(x, na.rm = T)/sqrt(length(x))
  dataset %>% select(-Replicate) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(target_vector, Conc.),
               names_to = 'pairs',
               values_to = 'fluorescence') %>% 
  group_by(Conc., target_vector, pairs) %>%
  summarise(average_fluorescence = mean(fluorescence),
            se = std.err(fluorescence)) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=Conc., y=average_fluorescence, color = target_vector))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_line()+
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=average_fluorescence-se, ymax = average_fluorescence+se), width = 0.2)+
  facet_wrap('pairs', scales = 'free')+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,5))+
  scale_x_log10()+
  theme_minimal()
}
```

```{r PERCENT CORRECT VISUALIZATION}
# Percent correct by concentration for all data
percent_correct_visualization = function(dataset, color){
  viz = dataset %>% mutate(across(concentration, round, 4)) %>%
    mutate_at('concentration', as.factor) %>% mutate(match = ifelse(predictions == labels, 1, 0)) %>% 
                          group_by(concentration) %>%
    summarize(num_correct = sum(match),
              total = n()) %>%
    mutate(percent_correct = (round(num_correct / total, 4)) * 100) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = concentration, y = percent_correct)) +
    geom_bar(stat = 'identity',
             fill = color) +
    geom_text(aes(label = percent_correct),
              vjust  = 1.5,
              color = 'white') +
    theme_classic() +
    ylab('Percent Correct') +
    xlab('Concentration') +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.001))
  
  return(viz)
}
```

```{r model training}
# Random forest model - dAb18
augmented_random_forest_model = function(dataset,
                                         target,
                                         k_folds,
                                         model_type,
                                         lower_thresh=0.9,
                                         upper_thresh=245){
  pred_concs = NULL
  
  # Thresholding around 1 ng/ml - corresponds to a threshold of ~20 pM
  dataset = dataset %>% filter(Conc. > lower_thresh & Conc. < upper_thresh) %>% select(-Replicate, -cAb10)
  folds = createFolds(dataset[[target]], k = k_folds)
  train_control = trainControl(method = "repeatedcv",
                               number = 5,
                               repeats = 3)
  model_formula = paste(target, '~', ".", "-Conc.") %>% as.formula()
  
  for (fold in 1:k_folds){
    train = dataset[-folds[[fold]],]
    test = dataset[folds[[fold]],]
    
    test_conc = test$Conc.
    
    preprocess = preProcess(train, method = c("center", "scale")) # , "YeoJohnson"
    train = predict(preprocess, train)
    test = predict(preprocess, test)
    
    x_test = test %>% select(-target)
    y_test = test[[target]]
    
    if (model_type == 'rf'){
      trained_model = train(model_formula,
                            data = train,
                            method = 'ranger',
                            importance = 'impurity',
                            trControl = train_control,
                            tuneLength = 15)

      predictions = predict(trained_model, x_test,
                            type = 'raw')
    }
    
    if (model_type == 'svmLinear'){
      trained_model = train(model_formula,
                            data = train,
                            method = 'svmLinear',
                            trControl = train_control,
                            tuneLength = 20)
      predictions = predict(trained_model, x_test,
                            type = 'raw')
    }
    
    if (model_type == 'svmRadial'){
      trained_model = train(model_formula,
                            data = train,
                            method = 'svmRadial',
                            trControl = train_control,
                            tuneLength = 20)
      predictions = predict(trained_model, x_test,
                            type = 'raw')
    }
    if (model_type == 'qda'){
      trained_model = train(model_formula,
                            data = train,
                            method = 'qda',
                            trControl = train_control,
                            tuneLength = 20)
      predictions = predict(trained_model, x_test,
                            type = 'raw')
    }
    
  # print(varImp(trained_model))
  accuracy = Accuracy(predictions, test[[target]])
  print(accuracy)
  
  pred_df = data.frame("concentration" = test_conc,
                       "predictions" = predictions,
                       "labels" = y_test)
  
  if (is.null(pred_concs)){
    pred_concs = pred_df
  }
  else {
    pred_concs = pred_concs %>% bind_rows(pred_concs, pred_df)
  }
  # print(trained_model)
  }
  pred_concs = pred_concs %>% arrange(desc(concentration))
  return(pred_concs)
}
```

```{r Augmented data}
# Ok so looks like random forests are doing the best here. Would it help us to generate some synthetic data?
synth_augmented_random_forest_model = function(dataset,
                                         target,
                                         k_folds,
                                         model_type,
                                         upper_thresh = 251,
                                         lower_thresh = 0.4,
                                         aug_ratio = 1){
  pred_concs = NULL
  # Provide this function a data frame with outlier's replaced with NA, then have it
  # split the data, impute the outliers with kNN, then augment the data
  # Thresholding around 1 ng/ml - corresponds to a threshold of 7.14 pM
  dataset = dataset %>% filter(Conc. > lower_thresh & Conc. < upper_thresh) %>% select(-Replicate)
  
  outlier_na_df = main_outliers_detection_function(dataset, 0.1, impute='na')
  
  folds = createFolds(dataset[[target]], k = k_folds)
  
  train_control = trainControl(method = "repeatedcv",
                               number = 5,
                               repeats = 3)
  
  model_formula = paste(target, '~', ".", "-Conc.") %>% as.formula()
  
  for (fold in 1:k_folds){
    train = dataset[-folds[[fold]],]
    test = dataset[folds[[fold]],]
    
    test_conc = test$Conc
    
    impute_rec = recipe(
      paste("target_vector", '~', '.') %>% as.formula(),
      data = train
    ) %>% step_rm(removals = 'Conc.')
    
    knn_imputed_test = impute_rec %>% 
      step_impute_knn(all_predictors(), neighbors = 3) %>% 
      prep(training=train) %>% 
      bake(test)
    
    knn_imputed_train = impute_rec %>% 
      step_impute_knn(all_predictors(), neighbors = 3) %>% 
      prep(training=train) %>% 
      bake(train)
    
    if (aug_ratio > 0){
      knn_impute_train_synth = syn(knn_imputed_train, m=aug_ratio)
      knn_impute_synth_aug = bind_rows(knn_imputed_train, knn_impute_train_synth$syn)
    }
    
    else if (aug_ratio == 0){
      knn_impute_synth_aug = knn_imputed_train
    }
    
    preprocess = preProcess(knn_impute_synth_aug, method = c("center", "scale"))
    proc_train = predict(preprocess, knn_impute_synth_aug)
    proc_test = predict(preprocess, knn_imputed_test)
    
    proc_x_test = proc_test %>% select(-target)
    proc_y_test = proc_test[[target]]
    
    trained_model = train(model_formula,
                          data = proc_train,
                          method = model_type,
                          importance='impurity',
                          tuneLength = 20)
    predictions = predict(trained_model, proc_x_test, type='raw')
    # if (model_type == 'rf'){
    #   trained_model = train(model_formula,
    #                         data = proc_train,
    #                         method = 'ranger',
    #                         importance = 'impurity',
    #                         trControl = train_control,
    #                         tuneLength = 15)
    # 
    #   predictions = predict(trained_model, proc_x_test,
    #                         type = 'raw')
    # }
    # 
    # if (model_type == 'svmLinear'){
    #   trained_model = train(model_formula,
    #                         data = proc_train,
    #                         method = 'svmLinear',
    #                         trControl = train_control,
    #                         tuneLength = 20)
    #   predictions = predict(trained_model, proc_x_test,
    #                         type = 'raw')
    # }
    # 
    # if (model_type == 'svmRadial'){
    #   trained_model = train(model_formula,
    #                         data = proc_train,
    #                         method = 'svmRadial',
    #                         trControl = train_control,
    #                         tuneLength = 20)
    #   predictions = predict(trained_model, proc_x_test,
    #                         type = 'raw')
    # }
    # 
    # if (model_type == 'qda'){
    #   trained_model = train(model_formula,
    #                         data = proc_train,
    #                         method = 'qda',
    #                         trControl = train_control,
    #                         tuneLength = 20)
    #   predictions = predict(trained_model, proc_x_test,
    #                         type = 'raw')
    # }
    
  # print(varImp(trained_model))
  accuracy = Accuracy(predictions, knn_imputed_test[[target]])
  print(accuracy)
  
  pred_df = data.frame("concentration" = test_conc,
                       "predictions" = predictions,
                       "labels" = proc_y_test)
  
  if (is.null(pred_concs)){
    pred_concs = pred_df
  }
  else {
    pred_concs = pred_concs %>% bind_rows(pred_concs, pred_df)
  }
  # print(trained_model)
  }
  pred_concs = pred_concs %>% arrange(desc(concentration))
  return(pred_concs)
}
```

```{r}
# Load the Iris dataset
data(iris)

# Prepare the data
X <- iris[, 1:4]   # Features
y <- as.numeric(iris$Species) - 1  # Convert species labels to 0, 1, 2

# Split the data into training and testing sets
set.seed(123)
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(iris), 0.7 * nrow(iris))
X_train <- X[train_indices, ]
y_train <- y[train_indices]
X_test <- X[-train_indices, ]
y_test <- y[-train_indices]

# Define XGBoost parameters for multi-class classification
params <- list(
  objective = "multi:softmax",  # Multi-class classification with softmax
  num_class = 4,                # Number of classes in the target variable
  eval_metric = "mlogloss",     # Evaluation metric for multi-class
  eta = 0.3,                    # Learning rate (shrinkage)
  max_depth = 6,                # Maximum depth of trees
  min_child_weight = 1,         # Minimum sum of instance weight needed in a child
  subsample = 1,                # Fraction of samples used for training
  colsample_bytree = 1,         # Fraction of features used for training in each tree
  nrounds = 100                 # Number of boosting rounds (trees)
)

# Convert data to DMatrix
dtrain <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_train, label = y_train)
dtest <- xgb.DMatrix(data = X_test, label = y_test)

# Train the XGBoost model
xgb_model <- xgboost(params = params, data = dtrain, nrounds = params$nrounds)

# Make predictions
predictions <- predict(xgb_model, dtest)

# Evaluate the model for multi-class classification
accuracy <- mean(predictions == y_test)
cat("Accuracy:", accuracy, "\n")
```
